atn7cc: Hablé, comí, salí: the regular forms
1ymls52: The simple past tells **finished** actions in a period that is already over. Verbs in **-er** and **-ir** share endings: _comí_ and _salí_, _comió_ and _salió_.
5gdr0c: The **written accent** is part of the form: _yo hablé_, _él habló_. Without it, _hablo_ is present. Always stress the last syllable: ha-**blé**, ha-**bló**.
1ip8qz9: With **nosotros**, -ar and -ir verbs look the same as in the present: _hablamos_, _salimos_. Context decides: _Ayer salimos tarde_ (past) / _Siempre salimos tarde_ (present).
1fuld0m: Without the accent, _llego_ is the present for yo. For él in the past: **llegó**.
8y5ynf: The tú form of the simple past has no final **-s**: **hablaste**.
hdwkuc: Events in order and spelling changes with yo
mqmqrb: The simple past goes with finished-time markers: **ayer**, **anoche**, **anteayer**, **el sábado pasado**, **la semana pasada**, **en 2021**. If the period hasn't finished yet (today, this week), remember you reviewed the perfect.
p88tz0: To tell a sequence, link the events with **primero**, **luego**, **después** and **al final**: _Primero desayunamos, luego subimos al bus y al final llegamos al parque._
1pxcbrs: Three types of verb change a letter only with **yo**, to keep the sound: **-car → -qué** (_buscar → busqué_), **-gar → -gué** (_llegar → llegué_), **-zar → -cé** (_empezar → empecé_). The other persons are regular: _buscó_, _llegaste_, _empezaron_.
1sbg74p: Look only at the yo form: if the verb ends in -car, -gar or -zar, the last letter changes. It's a spelling rule, not a pronunciation rule.
1vzqtxr: With yo, _-gar_ is written **-gué** to keep the sound of the g.
19gnao6: New stem and no accent: fui, hice, tuve…
1mqhy6t: The most frequent verbs have a **new stem** in the simple past and endings **without an accent**: _tuv-e_, _tuv-o_. Compare: _llegué_ and _llegó_ have an accent, but _tuve_ and _tuvo_ don't.
oizks5: **Ir** and **ser** have the same forms: _fui_, _fue_, _fueron_. Context decides: _Fui a Alajuela_ (ir, with **a** + place) / _Fue un día largo_ (ser, an evaluation).
1p8nsi6: **Hacer** changes c to z with él and ella: _hizo_, to keep the sound. And **decir** loses the i with ellos: _dijeron_, not _dijieron_.
1gsgie7: _Hacer_ with ella: **hizo**, with z and no accent.
7htxa1: Irregular verbs with a new stem take no accent: **estuve**.
rq5dpo: Some **-ir** verbs that change their stem in the present (_pido_, _duermo_) have another change in the simple past, but **only with él, ella, usted and ellos, ellas, ustedes**: **e** becomes **i** and **o** becomes **u**.
1dk7b3w: **e → i**: _pedir → pidió, pidieron_; also _servir_, _repetir_, _preferir_, _sentir_, _seguir_. **o → u**: _dormir → durmió, durmieron_; also _morir → murió_.
18emvy: With yo, tú, nosotros and vosotros nothing changes: _pedí_, _dormiste_, _servimos_. If in doubt, ask yourself: am I talking about someone else? Then check the vowel.
15o4hse: Remember the sentence _Él pidió y ellos durmieron_: it has both changes and the two persons where they happen.
1ytbkus: With ella, the e of _pedir_ becomes **i**: **pidió**.
1qqwub8: With **yo** there's no change: **dormí**. The o → u change is only for él and ellos.

1j99lju: In -ar verbs, the difference between the present for yo and the past for él is only the **stress**: _llego_ (LLE-go, present) and _llegó_ (lle-GÓ, past). If you stress the wrong syllable, you change the tense and the person.
3nbevi: The same happens with _compro / compró_, _paso / pasó_, _tomo / tomó_. When you talk about the past, lean on the **last** syllable and lengthen it slightly.
hfo9ar: With yo in the past the stress is also at the end: _llegué_, _compré_. The irregular forms (_tuve_, _hice_) are stressed on the second-to-last syllable, like most words.
ul0r6c: Always write the accent on the _-é_ and _-ó_ of regular verbs: without it, the reader sees a present. Irregular verbs with a new stem (_tuve_, _pudo_, _hizo_) never have one.
